frequency_question: What proportion of major structural reform bills pass all legislative stages and are signed into law within a 60-day calendar window from initial floor consideration?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan structural reform bills that require bicameral agreement and committee reconciliation; excludes standard appropriations, continuing resolutions, and non-controversial technical corrections.

cases.name: TARP / Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008

provenance_note: claims 35 cases from only 7 named (5.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 7 named representative fast-track hits; estimated 35 total major legislative pushes attempting sub-60-day passage in modern congressional history
known_gaps: Excludes minor non-controversial bills that bypass committee friction; focuses strictly on complex structural reforms attempting rapid passage.
skeleton: Fast-tracked emergency or high-priority consensus bills passing within 60 days divided by total attempted major legislative overhauls requiring multi-committee coordination
multiplier: 7 hits out of 35 major attempted structural overhauls spanning 1995-2024 that faced a compressed timeline under 60 days
validity_reason: Congressional procedural rules and polarization dynamics remain stable across multi-year congressional terms.
